- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.28) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or 10% below recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.17), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves after negative sentiment; add 1–3% buffer to forecast when sentiment dips below 0.00.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early-term (1–7 day) decline; apply 1–2% upward adjustment to first 3–5 days if sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.17), model exhibits “choppy” behavior; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying trend correction.
